baseline.convention: sqrt(pi r / (2c)) elliptic group operations for an equivalence class of c elements, negation included. The cost model's sqrt(pi r / 4) (jacobian_transfer::cost) is the c = 2 case, so a class enters as sqrt(c / 2); certificate v1 divided that reference by sqrt(c), counted negation twice and sat 0.5 bit low (Amendment 3). isogeny_degree_search::rho_reference uses sqrt(pi r / 2) (no equivalence class), a factor sqrt 2 higher, and is not used
baseline.equivalence_class_reason: negation and the order-3 endomorphism of j = 0 (p = 1 mod 3): classes of size 6

candidate.label: Tate/Weil pairing into F_(q^k)^*, k = embedding degree of r

checks.evidence: one element of F_(q^k) has 5.342e3 bits (1 TiB = 8.80e12 bits): above that the pairing cannot be evaluated and the price below is a formal extrapolation of the cost model
checks.name: pairing_target_element_storable

checks.evidence: #E = q would put the curve in the scope of Smart's attack, which this tool does not cover
checks.name: anomalous_curve

rows.formula: the pairing is defined by the curve; no auxiliary curve or cover is constructed (the auxiliary point of the Weil pairing is not needed for the Tate pairing)
two pairing evaluations: log2(2 * log2(r) * 12 * M(k log2 q)); MILLER_MULTS_PER_BIT is a placeholder that never decides a verdict
balanced with the linear algebra in L[1/3] algorithms; priced together below

conservative end of the band: min(L_N[1/3, 1.9230] with o(1) dropped, weighted by M(k log2 q) = 2^194.4; generic rho/Pohlig-Hellman in the order-r subgroup of F_(q^k)^* = 2^242.0); N = q^k. The attacker-favourable end (c = 1.5263, unweighted) is 2^138.7
the logarithm of e(G,S)^d to base e(G,S) is d mod r: recovery is free; one scalar multiplication on E verifies it

costs.unit: log2 bit operations (frozen formula model; measured rows say so)

instance_checks.evidence: r passes Miller-Rabin to bases 2..53 (Probable); [r]G = O, G != O, so G has exact order r
instance_checks.name: subgroup_order_is_prime_and_annihilates_generator

instance_checks.evidence: #E = cofactor * r = q + 1 - t, Hasse bound holds, two seeded random points are annihilated by #E (evidence for the recorded order, not a point-count proof)
instance_checks.name: order_consistency

instance_checks.evidence: curve_traits::compute run live on this instance
instance_checks.name: traits_record

evaluation.reason: map Theorem, subgroup arithmetic, priced 44.5 bits below the matched baseline, past the 8-bit margin

invariants.class_invariant: the embedding degree depends only on q and r, which every curve of the isogeny class shares
invariants.embedding_method: least k <= 1000 with r | q^k - 1 (ascending scan)

price_band.reading: robustly below: even the conservative price is under the matched rho

map.explicit_formulas: Miller's algorithm; no generic pairing is implemented in the repository (mov_attack ships k = 2 supersingular only)

notes: reading of the verdict: it is relative. It compares the conservative price of a discrete logarithm in F_(q^k) (2^194.4 operations: generic NFS constant, o(1) dropped, weighted by the field-multiplication cost) with the matched rho on <G> (2^238.9). `class-weak` means the first is below the second by at least the 8-bit model margin, i.e. a conservative pairing price below rho under this model; it does not say the curve is weak at any absolute security level, and `no weakness found in scope` does not say it is strong
open_obligations: implement a generic Tate pairing and execute it on the generator (only k = 2 supersingular exists in mov_attack.rs)
replace the L[1/3] lower bound by a priced index-calculus pipeline for F_(q^k) (quasi-polynomial algorithms for small characteristic are not modeled)

antecedents.evidence: gcd(q, r) = 1, so the embedding degree is defined
antecedents.name: r_does_not_divide_q

antecedents.evidence: least k <= 1000 with r | q^k - 1 (ascending scan)
antecedents.name: embedding_degree_exact

antecedents.evidence: curve_traits::compute reports the same embedding degree or the same lower bound
antecedents.name: agrees_with_curve_traits_record

subgroup_preservation.argument: for k the embedding degree the Tate-Lichtenbaum pairing is non-degenerate (Frey-Ruck 1994), so some S makes e(G, S) a primitive r-th root of unity: the image of <G> has order r. Not executed
subgroup_preservation.method: arithmetic: Frey-Ruck non-degeneracy of the Tate pairing at k = ord_r(q)

verdict_basis: pairing (MOV/Frey-Ruck): subgroup carried, map Theorem, priced total 44.5 bits below the matched baseline (margin 8 bits); a statement relative to rho on <G> under the frozen formula model, not a claim about absolute security
